en.title: Subarrays with at Least k Pairs of Equal Elements
en.description:
A pair means two distinct indices i<j within the subarray whose elements are equal. Count the non-empty contiguous subarrays that contain at least k pairs.

This site's standard input/output is stated explicitly; ranges not given by the source are all marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n k, and the second line contains n elements; 1≤n≤100000, 1≤a[i],k≤10⁹.
en.explanation: Example 1: the whole array has exactly 10 pairs, and every shorter range has too few, so the answer is 1. Example 2: the valid ranges are indices [0,5], [0,6], [1,6], and [2,6], so the answer is 4. Example 3: the elements are distinct and there are no equal pairs, so the answer is 0.
hints: Maintain the window and its frequencies with two pointers. A new element adds as many pairs as its previous frequency; once the window satisfies k, the current right end and every farther right end are valid for this left end, so count them and then remove the left end.
